title: Measurement: the host consent record grants nothing a clone could carry, and a changed choice clears its grant
summary: TSK-0034, toward ACC-0054, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit 2ea341a, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. lib/consent-record.mjs reads the ignored consent record under the existing consent schema before any prompt, and lib/connection-inspection.mjs gains inspectWithConsent, which reuses a recorded inspection answer and asks only a host with none. WHAT GRANTS. A record grants only when it is valid, its location passes the existing coverageState check, and Git gives a definite answer that no clone can carry it. gitProtection runs from the record's own directory, so Git finds the repository that really holds it (the project, a parent repository, a linked worktree whose .git is a file, or a nested repository), and asks three things: whether the record is in the index, whether it is in HEAD, and whether that repository's effective rules ignore it (git check-ignore). Only ignored, or no repository at all, lets the record be trusted or written. Tracked, committed, not ignored and inconclusive all grant nothing, and a record in any of those states is never written over. Writes ask even when the file is absent. Missing, unreadable, invalid and unprotected records grant nothing. THE THREE GRANTS. Inspection, model use for one exact provider and model, and research use for tavily are written, read and cleared separately. Only true or false is recorded. A closed input or empty answer grants nothing and records nothing. INVALIDATION. Whenever a read sees a current choice different from the one a grant names, or no choice, the grant is removed from the record under the lock, so model A to B to A asks again, and research tavily to none (or unset) to tavily asks again. clearGrants is the call a choice writer makes in the same step. HOW IT IS OBSERVED. test/helpers/access-recorder.mjs, the harness of EVD-0125, watches Pi's agent directory on the second host and the credential variables ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY, and makes every network call record and throw. The second host holds a stored openai key in auth.json and sentinel values in the environment. Counts are taken at every prompt and after every credential access, so each prompt is compared with the state just before it. CLONE CONTROLS. (1) PROJECT-LOCAL STATE: the first host grants all three and an unchanged relaunch asks nothing. The project is committed, git ls-files shows exactly .gitignore and .pi/kiln.json, and git clone produces the copy. On the second host the record is absent, and all three prompts reopen with zero credential access before the inspection prompt and none added before the model-use or research prompts. (2) PER-USER STATE: the clone derives the second host's own root from a different LOCALAPPDATA and XDG_STATE_HOME. The record there is absent and the same prompt sequence holds. Git reports no repository for the per-user root. (3) THE POSITIVE CONTROL, in every clone control: after each yes, the recorder sees the auth.json read, the model-use credential read and the research credential read, so the zero counts at each prompt are absences rather than blind spots. No network attempt was recorded. NEGATIVE CONTROLS. (R1) A valid, fully granted record force-added past the ignore block and committed reaches the clone inside the ignore rules. It is read as tracked and grants nothing, all three prompts reopen before any credential access, the answers are not written, and the file bytes are unchanged. (R5) After git rm --cached without a commit, the first host reads the record as committed and refuses to write it. A clone of that HEAD still receives the granted record, which grants nothing there, with the same prompt sequence. The first host trusts its record again only once the removal is committed. The linked-worktree test asserts the same, then asserts the record is trusted after the committed removal. (R6) A project with no .git of its own inside a parent repository that does not ignore it: an answer is not written there (reason not-ignored, with no file created), and a granted record placed there by hand is not trusted. After the parent runs git add -A, commits and is cloned, the clone receives the record and it grants nothing, with the same prompt sequence. A parent repository that ignores the runtime directory lets the record be written and reused. OTHER TESTS. Unchanged local reuse, recorded declines, non-answers, separate grants, provider-only changes, a model choice removed, explicit clearing, and a choice that omits model or research being refused so a grant cannot be cleared by omission. LIMITS. (R4) Where Git is unavailable or gives no definite answer, no saved answer is trusted and none is written, so an unchanged project is asked on every launch. The answer's result carries notRemembered, which tells the operator the answer applies to this run only and why. This was tested with a missing Git binary. (R7) Protection is checked against the current checkout on each read. A checkout of another branch is checked against that branch's HEAD, and older commits are not examined. (R2) The invalidation and clearGrants behaviour is proved at the API. No choice writer exists yet: the model selection writer (TSK-0036) and the research choice writer (TSK-0035) must call clearGrants when they change a choice, and nothing yet shows they do. (R3) A second clone on the same machine for the same user in per-user state shares the local record keyed by the committed project ID. That is the same operator on the same host, and ACC-0054's case is a machine with no local record. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. The launch path and the choice writers are not connected, so ACC-0054 is not evaluated here. No real model or research request was made: the credential uses in the controls are reads of the variable. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Five changes each failed the tests: inspection standing always granted, inspection before the prompt, the index check removed from the read, the HEAD check removed, and not-ignored treated as safe. CI had not run on 2ea341a when this was recorded, and its result is added separately.

facts.tests: test/consent-record.test.mjs 17 tests and test/connection-inspection.test.mjs 7 tests: 24 pass, 0 fail
facts.recorder: test/helpers/access-recorder.mjs rooted at the second host's Pi agent directory; watched variables ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY; network calls record and throw
facts.grant-condition: valid record, coverageState covered, and gitProtection ignored or no-repository
facts.git-questions: from the record's directory: ls-files --error-unmatch (index), rev-parse --verify -q HEAD^{commit} then ls-tree HEAD (commit), check-ignore (effective rules); LC_ALL=C, no GIT_* variables passed, core.fsmonitor=false
facts.clone-project-local: committed files exactly .gitignore and .pi/kiln.json; record absent in the clone; three prompts reopened; zero watched access at the inspection prompt, none added before the model-use or research prompts
facts.clone-per-user: second host root from a different LOCALAPPDATA and XDG_STATE_HOME; record absent; same prompt sequence; per-user root reported as no repository
facts.positive-control: after each yes: auth.json read, one model-use credential read, one research credential read; no network attempt
facts.negative-r1-force-added: valid fully granted record in the clone, inside the ignore rules, read as tracked; three prompts reopened before credential access; answers not written (reason tracked); file bytes unchanged
facts.negative-r5-staged-removal: origin reads committed and refuses to write; clone of that HEAD receives the granted record and it grants nothing, same prompt sequence; trusted again only after the removal is committed; linked worktree (.git is a file) asserts the same
facts.negative-r6-parent-repository: project without .git in a parent repository that does not ignore it: nothing written (reason not-ignored), hand-placed granted record not trusted; after parent add -A, commit and clone, the record grants nothing, same prompt sequence; a parent that ignores the runtime directory allows write and reuse
facts.invalidation: model A to B clears A's grant from the record and B to A asks again; provider change and model removal clear; research tavily to none or unset clears and tavily again asks; inspection unaffected
facts.limit-r4-no-git: missing Git binary: record read as unverified, nothing written, an unchanged project asked again; result carries NOT_REMEMBERED.unverified
facts.limit-r7-branches: protection is checked against the current checkout's index and HEAD on each read; another branch is checked against its own HEAD when checked out; older commits are not examined
facts.limit-r2-writers: clearGrants has no caller; TSK-0035 and TSK-0036 choice writers do not exist
facts.scope-r3-same-host: same user, same machine, per-user state: clones share the local record keyed by the committed project ID
facts.mutations: 5 of 5 killed locally on Windows: inspection standing always granted, inspection before the prompt, index check removed, HEAD check removed, not-ignored treated as safe; the last two restored byte-identical by sha256, the first three were in earlier versions of the files since edited
facts.full-suite-local: npm test on Windows: 1475 tests, 1470 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped

omissions.reason: The research choice writer, the model selection writer and their clearGrants calls do not exist, and the launch path is not connected. This is component proof, and ACC-0054 is evaluated once those paths are connected.
CI had not run on 2ea341a when this was recorded. Only the local Windows results are recorded here, and the CI result is added separately.
The credential uses in the controls are variable reads. No model or research request was made.
Only the current checkout's index and HEAD are checked. A record committed on another branch or in older history is not examined until that branch is checked out.
Git is asked from the record's own directory, which handles a nested repository by construction, but no test covers one.
